articles.title: Most disability claims get denied. Here's why — and what Social Security is actually looking for.
articles.summary: The SSDI process can be difficult to navigate. Knowing what Social Security looks for can help.
articles.body:
Navigating the application process for Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) can be difficult. People wait around six months on average just to get a first decision, according to the latest available government data .

Even then, that initial decision is more often than not a 'no.' Among claims filed from 2014 through 2023, 68% were denied, according to the latest available government data, either on medical grounds or for technical reasons, such as not having worked recently enough to be insured.

And approval doesn't mean payment straight away: benefits don't begin until five months after the date Social Security decides a disability started — a waiting period that often overlaps with the time a claim spends under review, though not always.

The bipartisan We Can't Wait Act , introduced by Rep. Carol Miller of West Virginia and Rep. Tom Suozzi of New York on Sept. 2, aims to address that wait by allowing SSDI beneficiaries to receive payments immediately in exchange for a "modestly reduced" monthly benefit. The bill has been backed by more than two dozen organizations as part of the We Can't Wait Coalition, including the National Organization of Social Security Claimants' Representatives (NOSSCR).

However, some disability rights groups have raised concerns, including The Arc of the United States, a leading nonprofit advocating for and supporting people with intellectual and developmental disabilities. It tells Yahoo News that any benefit cuts would "leave many SSDI beneficiaries worse off in the long run."

Here's what applicants should know when filing a claim.

Why is the approval rate for SSDI so low?

About 18% to 21% of SSDI applicants have their initial claims approved, according to the Social Security Administration 's latest analysis of applicants from 2014 to 2023.

SSDI applicants face the challenge of not just proving that they are disabled, but also that their condition has kept them from working, or is expected to keep them from working, for at least 12 months, or that it is terminal. People need to prove they qualify on both medical grounds (for example, their condition is severe enough) and technical reasons (that they have worked enough to be eligible).

"The low initial approval rate likely reflects the complexity of proving both medical and non-medical eligibility," Shannon Benton, the executive director of the Senior Citizens League, told Yahoo News. "Claims may be denied when medical evidence is incomplete or does not clearly establish the severity and functional impact of a condition."

The lengthy application asks for details about an applicant's medical conditions, their last five years of work history and their medical providers. But even a carefully completed form may not capture what Social Security is really looking for.

"Many initial applications do not contain enough evidence about the claimant's functional limitations," said Kelly Blad, president of the National Association of Disability Representatives (NADR), whose membership includes nearly 700 disability representatives nationwide. "Medical records may document diagnoses, medications and treatment, but say very little about how long the person can sit, stand or walk; whether they can concentrate and remain on task; how often they would miss work; or whether they can function reliably five days a week."

That burden of proof falls hardest on people who may struggle to carry it. "So even folks who really should qualify will often answer a question wrong, or fail to get the right records in at the right time," Stephanie Akpa, head of policy and public affairs at Atticus, a company that connects disability applicants with lawyers and helps people apply for and win disability benefits, told Yahoo News. "If there's a shadow of a doubt that you qualify, the agency will generally deny you and then expect it to get sorted out on appeal."

In August, the SSA took steps to speed up SSDI decisions for people with particularly serious issues, adding 14 conditions to the existing 300 on its Compassionate Allowances list, a fast-track program that applies to both SSDI and SSI.

While the additions were welcomed by disability advocates, not all conditions are treated equally by the SSDI system. People with conditions that fluctuate or rely on symptoms that are hard to measure objectively tend to face tougher odds at a successful application.

"These may include chronic pain, fibromyalgia, migraines, long COVID, mental health conditions and disorders involving fatigue," Blad said. "These conditions can be profoundly disabling, but their effects may not be fully reflected in laboratory testing or a brief medical examination."

Other conditions, due to their severity, are significantly more likely to be approved.

"If you have ALS, Alzheimer's, metastatic cancer, or a recent heart transplant, the system understands that you almost certainly can't work, and, barring paperwork errors or missed records, folks generally get approved," Akpa said.

This is not as clear-cut when it comes to conditions that vary in severity for each person.

"Where it's hard is conditions that are moderate for some people but utterly debilitating for others, like early-stage cancers, back problems, diabetes, and really any mental health condition," Akpa said.

Mental health claims also fall into this category, which can lead to complications, Blad said. Mental disorders made up 13.5% of all disabled-worker awards in 2024, according to SSA data , despite being one of the most common conditions among applicants.

"The condition itself may make it hard to seek care, keep appointments, complete paperwork or communicate effectively," Blad said. "Unfortunately, those gaps can be interpreted as evidence that the condition is not severe."

While there's no guaranteed path to approval, experts say thorough documentation, awareness of fast-track options, legal representation and persistence if denied can strengthen an applicant's case.

"Applicants can generally improve their chances by providing thorough medical documentation, responding promptly to SSA requests and seeking qualified assistance if their claim is denied," Benton said.

Details are also key. Blad said applicants should ask treating providers to document functional limitations, not just diagnoses, detailing bad days and the help they need from others. She added that applicants should notify SSA immediately if they have a terminal illness or another exceptionally serious condition, as some claims may qualify for expedited processing through programs such as Compassionate Allowances .

Darcy Milburn, social security and health care policy director at The Arc, said that claimants should seek legal help if they feel they need it during the process.

"The complexity of the SSDI application process is an enormous barrier to accessing urgently needed benefits. It can be extremely difficult for someone to get through the application process without the assistance of a lawyer."

Above all, experts caution that a denial isn't automatically the end of the road. Applicants generally have 60 days to appeal and should do so rather than start over, Blad said.

"In fact, folks who get denied and do appeal, with legal representation, have a higher than 50% success rate, higher than any other appellate system we as lawyers know of," Akpa said.

articles.title: Squishies, brainrot and an 'emotional support Eleven': Gen Alpha backpacks offer a peek into their world
articles.summary: Kids open their backpacks to reveal the school supplies, squishies, beauty products, charms and oddball treasures Gen Alpha carries.
articles.body:
From lucky pencils and lip gloss to squishies and a soccer ball, the contents reveal what these kids love, need and refuse to leave home without.

New clothes. Supplies. Lunches. Sports schedules. Tracking apps. Walking group text threads.

A new school year comes with a seemingly endless checklist. According to Yahoo's Back-to-School Trends Report , one item generates more search interest than anything else: the backpack.

Backpacks have long been a form of self-expression — Disney princesses, superheroes, sports teams. For Gen Alpha, the customization is even more layered: charms, sushi key chains, Liila dolls, plush clips and danglecore transform the outside of a bag into its own mood board.

Inside, the personality continues. Alongside notebooks, laptops and school ID's, you'll find Laneige lip gloss, Touchland hand sanitizer and Hero blemish patches. There's lots of LoveShackFancy , not to mention Squishmallows, Pokémon , Roblox brainrot and squishies .

Then there's the unpredictable: The giant Tootsie Roll container, which seems almost retro. The "mistake paper" ball that grows and grows. Also — my fave — a "secret society" ID card.

"You never know when you're gonna need something or if your friend needs something," Tootsie Roll aficionado and prepared-for-anything Claire, 12, tells Yahoo.

She's one of 11 kids, ages 7 to 12, from across the country who agreed to give us a backpack tour. Here's what they stash inside and clip outside.

Everyone needs a Claire, the friend guided by the "be prepared" motto.

Wearing an Alex Warren T-shirt, the Pennsylvania seventh grader shows me her "purpley-blue" JanSport, a smaller version of last year's pack, which hurt her back.

Inside are the usual school basics — a laptop, an accordion binder and a "C" pencil case. As she talks, a stack of Post-its falls out of the bag.

"I like to have like two, three packs of sticky notes on hand," she tells me, adding that she carries the same pink "lucky pencil" she's used on all tests since fifth grade.

The "just in case" stuff: hair ties and bobby pins, Touchland hand sanitizer, scissors and a "school emergency kit" with mints, "Gummy Burst"-scented deodorant, Kayali perfume, e.l.f. lip gloss, Invisalign rubber bands and a broken nail file.

"Just, like, kind of anything I need," she says. "I can grab it throughout the day."

Other distinctly Claire items: an oversize and loaded Tootsie Roll container won at a bat mitzvah that she dips into if she's "feeling down or … just like tired," The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes from the Hunger Games series ("I've read all the other ones") and a green bunny squishy with the "perfect texture."

On the outside? A lone purple crocheted heart, chosen because it's her favorite color. ( Tweens love lavender. )

"I have, like, a system with my stuff," the Florida seventh grader says.

One look at her navy JanSport confirms it: Haidyn's folders are arranged in class-period order. History is first, reading second, with less-used materials tucked further back and everyday essentials — laptop, lunchbox and calculator — within easy reach.

The front pouch holds a pencil box with a ROYGBIV array of writing tools and a handful of school IDs in case "I lose one or something," which seems doubtful given her system. In a side pocket, she keeps a pencil, pen, dry-erase marker and hairbrush for easy access.

Some Gen Alpha must-haves: a smartphone, a hot-selling Owala water bottle , sunglasses, Native deodorant, lip gloss and Trident Vibes gum, which she keeps at the top of her bag.

Meanwhile, her backpack's look follows a system too. According to her mom, it "has to hang low or else it's not cool."

The North Carolina seventh grader keeps things simple.

He's on his second Baseball Lifestyle 101 ice cream-drip backpack with a matching water bottle, though his mom says he likes ice cream more than baseball. (From what I've seen on social media — including a recent goal — soccer seems to be his sport.)

Which brings me to the fact that he didn't want to talk to me about his backpack, which I can fully relate to.

His mom tells me he travels light because his school has a no-homework policy and students don't have to haul supplies back and forth. The only things that come home are his Minecraft lunch box, which he's been using for the last few years, and a folder.

He's also deep into Michael Jackson, reading a biography at night and drawing his own versions of the King of Pop's album covers.

And that crumpled ball? Reagan and his classmates make them out of "mistake paper and do-overs," including rejected art.

Did someone say soccer ? City kid Edie, a sixth grader from Massachusetts, makes her love of the sport known.

"In my backpack, I always have to have my water bottle, soccer ball and cleats," she tells me. "They're most important to me because I love to play soccer and you always need to hydrate."

Her bright pink Nike Elite backpack is covered in empowering words like "courage" and "strength." The positive messaging continues inside with a pouch that reads, "You're beautiful, don't change."

Inside, there is a mix of school-day basics: notebooks, folders and a striped pencil case. There are also some just-in-case items: Kleenex, Band-Aids, hair ties, ibuprofen and three colorful NeeDoh Cool Cats squishies.

Nobody is left wondering who Beau is rooting for.

The nearly 8-year-old second grader from Texas carries a black Old Navy bag featuring Lionel Messi under a giant "G.O.A.T." banner. A gold FIFA World Cup trophy key chain, purchased at a soccer jersey store in London, hangs on the front. The soccer theme continues with a black, white and gold Nike water bottle.

A gold Lego robot key chain, bought at the Lego Store at the Philadelphia International Airport, adds a non-soccer note. He's actually downgraded his danglecore this year.

"Last year, I had a lot of metal key chains, and they hit together and it was annoying," he shared.

Inside, everything is straightforward second-grade school stuff — a folder, a bento box and the basics — making the message on the outside even more pronounced: Messi all the way.

This sixth grader from Ohio scored LoveShackFancy x Yoobi for Target before much of the collection sold out.

Kate has the floral backpack, a matching pencil pouch, notebooks and a pouch for her Chromebook charger and earbuds.

Bows — a signature part of the brand's ultrafeminine, romantic aesthetic — are pinned across the front pouch. Another bow dangles alongside bear and rabbit plush key chains.

Her water bottle fits the trend-aware vibe too: a Starbucks x Dandy Worldwide Road Trip bottle. A Yondr pouch keeps her phone locked away during the school day.

In the bag, she's carrying Small Steps: The Year I Got Polio , "the book that I'm reading right now," plus her folder for chorus and computer.

Audrey's JanSport looks pretty neutral on the outside. Inside, it's a colorful wonderland.

The Pennsylvania fifth grader is prepared like her sister Claire, but her version leans more toward self-care. She has five lip glosses, a Crocs x Touchland hand sanitizer, a compact mirror, a brush and hair ties, perfume, a mini first-aid kit and Scope.

"If I have tea in the morning or matcha, I have mouthwash," she says.

That stash sits alongside squishies (dumplings and NeeDoh), a rubber duck and a Stranger Things Funko Bitty Pop.

"It's my emotional support Eleven," she explains. ( Millie Bobby Brown is also a Gen Alpha fave .)

Her books include Frindle for class and a signed copy of Small Town Monsters . Of the latter, she says with a wink, "What I like about this is I have this nice little bow charm [bookmark] on a horror book."

On the outside, Audrey has key chains including her name in beads, a heart and a cupcake. She isn't over the loss of an earlier one.

"I had Tarte lip gloss on this, but it fell off and I lost it forever," she says. "I'm sad about that."

"I have an Apple AirTag because this year I'm walking home since I'm now in fifth grade," Lucy tells me.

The New Jersey fifth grader has confidence to spare, so much so that when her younger sister got shy during her own backpack tour, Lucy answered those questions too.

That self-assurance carries into what she packs. Lucy's neutral All in Motion backpack contrasts with the frillier LoveShackFancy x Yoobi supplies inside. Her nonessential must-haves include Laneige Peach Glaze lip serum ("so my lips will never get dry") and hand sanitizer ("in case I touch anything gross").

I needed a fainting couch after hearing how she selected her reading material: "My teacher said to bring a book, so I chose P.S. I Like You because I like romance," she says.

The Taylor Swift fan also leaves me with her thoughts on what her friends will have in their bags this year: "Owalas, squishies, fidgets and Fugglers ," she predicts.

This is Lucy's sister, and while she's a little shyer, she's living in her own bright and colorful world.

The New Jersey second grader's school supplies, housed in a cherry- and heart-covered Locker Club bag, are basically a lineup of favorite things: a blue axolotl pencil case, a Squishmallows spiral notebook, a metallic rainbow composition book, light blue scissors and strawberry hand sanitizer.

Her logic is refreshingly simple: axolotls, Squishmallows, pink, blue and strawberries. She likes what she likes.

"Me and my friend play this game where we are in this secret society thing, and we have like an ID," Dash tells me, holding it up.

That is just one thing the fourth grader from California has a story about. Even his key chains — sushi, corn and an NFL London Games charm — on his JanSport come with origin stories he's happy to share.

One marks a reading marathon, during which he says he was "one of the best in the class." Another came from a perfect-attendance streak. He's also in a school play, which explains the pink highlighter he uses to mark his lines.

Yes, there's a homework folder and math book, but I'm more excited by his hand-drawn "Mecha-Tech" pictures and the "Star Dollars" he earns at his after-school program and trades in for prizes, including a Pikachu figure he holds up.

Then there's a Roblox brainrot figure that he found on the ground.

"It is a spaghetti toilet," he says with a smile.

Rachel says the things in her backpack "mostly reflect who I am" — especially her love of singing, her friends and family and "how messy I am."

On the outside of the New York sixth grader's Simple Modern bag are some of her "most prized possessions": a Liila toy key chain her mother bought her and a blue plush Rhode Island key chain she bought on a trip there.

Inside, band and chorus binders hold her sheet music — fitting for a kid who wants to be a singer-songwriter. She also carries plenty of pencils because hers tend to "spontaneously go missing," plus a planner with an encouraging message on each page. There's also a key in a Hello Kitty wrap.

Her toiletries stash is pure middle school: Laneige lip balm, La Roche-Posay sunscreen and moisturizer, blemish patches, Kleenex and a scrunchie.

"It can be very useful for school and day-to-day life," she says. "And if you don't believe me, ask my friends. Most of them have something like this as well."

articles.title: Shopee deve instalar novo centro de distribuição no Sul de Minas | G1
articles.standfirst: Estrutura será instalada em galpão de aproximadamente 14 mil metros quadrados no Distrito Industrial de Pouso Alegre. Operação está prevista para começar no início de 2027.
articles.summary: Estrutura será instalada em galpão de aproximadamente 14 mil metros quadrados no Distrito Industrial de Pouso Alegre. Operação está prevista para começar no início de 2027.
articles.body:
A Shopee pretende instalar um novo centro de distribuição em Pouso Alegre , no Sul de Minas. A previsão é que a operação comece no início de 2027. A informação foi divulgada pela prefeitura nesta quinta-feira (17).

O novo centro ficará em um galpão de aproximadamente 14 mil metros quadrados no Distrito Industrial da cidade. O imóvel já foi locado pela empresa e anteriormente abrigava um centro de distribuição da Cremer, fabricante de produtos para a área da saúde.

Segundo a prefeitura, a Shopee já mantém uma operação em Pouso Alegre, mas a nova unidade permitirá a transferência para um espaço maior. A estrutura conta com docas e instalações destinadas ao recebimento, à movimentação e à distribuição de mercadorias.

Até o momento, não foram divulgados o valor do investimento nem o número de empregos que serão gerados pela nova operação. Também não há previsão oficial para o início das contratações.

Distrito Industrial de Pouso Alegre — Foto: Prefeitura de Pouso Alegre

Pouso Alegre está a cerca de 200 quilômetros de São Paulo e 390 quilômetros de Belo Horizonte e é cortada pela BR-381, a Fernão Dias, uma das principais rodovias de ligação entre os dois estados.

A localização é um dos fatores que colocam o município no mapa de empresas dos setores industrial e logístico. A cidade também integra uma região com acesso a importantes mercados consumidores do Sudeste.

De acordo com a prefeitura, Minas Gerais é o segundo estado com maior número de vendedores ativos na Shopee no Brasil. O município afirma ainda que o estado concentra um número expressivo de consumidores da plataforma.

Shopee deve instalar novo centro de distribuição e ampliar operação logística em Pouso Alegre, MG — Foto: Prefeitura de Pouso Alegre

Ainda conforme divulgado pela gestão municipal, a chegada da nova estrutura ocorre em um momento de expansão da operação logística da Shopee no Brasil. A empresa vem ampliando sua rede de centros de distribuição para acompanhar o crescimento das compras realizadas pela plataforma e contribuir para a redução dos prazos de entrega.

articles.title: Extorsão com vídeos íntimos: homem é preso no Piauí por crimes no CE | G1
articles.standfirst: Denúncias contra o suspeito foram registradas no estado do Ceará. Homem foi preso em São Raimundo Nonato e permanece à disposição da Justiça.
articles.summary: Investigado por extorsão com vídeos íntimos contra mulheres do Ceará é preso em São Raimundo Nonato após mandado de prisão preventiva da Justiça cearense.
articles.body:
Viatura da Polícia Civil do Piauí — Foto: PC-PI

Um homem, que não teve a identidade divulgada, foi preso nesta quinta-feira (17), em São Raimundo Nonato , no Sudeste do Piauí, suspeito de gravar vídeos íntimos de mulheres sem autorização e usar as imagens para extorquir as vítimas.

O suspeito era alvo de um mandado de prisão preventiva expedido pela Justiça do Ceará, estado onde as denunciantes moram. Segundo a investigação, ele mora no Piauí e utilizava as redes sociais para entrar em contato com as vítimas e realizar chamadas de vídeos com elas.

Durante as ligações, ele convencia as vítimas a expor o conteúdo íntimo. De acordo com a polícia, o homem armazenava as imagens e ameaçava divulgar os vídeos para extorquir as vítimas. A polícia não divulgou o número de denúncias formalizadas sobre o caso.

Segundo o delegado José Wellington, da Delegacia Seccional de São Raimundo Nonato, não há registros de denúncias contra o suspeito no Piauí até a última reportagem desta reportagem.

O preso permanece à disposição da Justiça.

*Eduarda Barradas, estagiária sob supervisão de Lucas Marreiros.

articles.title: Apreensão de cigarros em Itatiaia: carga irregular é interceptada | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo o Gabinete de Segurança Institucional do Estado do Rio de Janeiro (GSI-RJ), foram inconsistências na documentação apresentada e informações divergentes sobre a procedência da carga.
articles.summary: A apreensão de cigarros em Itatiaia ocorreu após o GSI-RJ identificar divergências na carga de 5.700 maços, agora sob análise da Receita Federal.
articles.body:
Carga irregular com mais de 5 mil maços de cigarro é apreendida em Itatiaia — Foto: Divulgação/GSI-RJ

Uma carga irregular com mais de 5 mil maços de cigarro foi apreendida em Itatiaia (RJ). O caso aconteceu na quarta-feira (16) mas, só foi divulgada nesta sexta-feira (18).

Segundo o Gabinete de Segurança Institucional do Estado do Rio de Janeiro (GSI-RJ), o carro recebeu ordem de parada ao passar pela área externa do Posto Fiscal de Nhangapi. A ação contou com agentes da Operação Foco.

Ainda de acordo com o GSI-RJ, durante as buscas, foram apreendidos 5.700 maços de cigarro. Os agentes também identificaram inconsistências na documentação apresentada pelo motorista e informações divergentes sobre a procedência da carga.

Todo o material apreendido foi retido e encaminhado para à Receita Federal para a análise da documentação, procedência e regularidade dos produtos.

Até a publicação desta reportagem, não se sabia se o motorista do carro havia ficado preso.

articles.title: Anne Frank: história e curiosidades do diário alvo de polêmica | G1
articles.standfirst: Influenciadora classificou a obra como 'vitimista' durante a 28ª Bienal do Livro de São Paulo. Museu do Holocausto e Federação Israelita repudiaram afirmação.
articles.summary: Após críticas na Bienal do Livro de SP, conheça a história de Anne Frank e curiosidades sobre o diário que narra os horrores do Holocausto.
articles.body:
O Diário de Anne Frank , um dos livros mais conhecidos sobre o Holocausto, voltou ao centro do debate no Brasil depois que uma influenciadora classificou a obra como "vitimista" durante a 28ª Bienal Internacional do Livro de São Paulo.

Em um vídeo publicado no TikTok, o perfil @JovemLiaa abordou uma visitante do evento e pediu que ela apontasse suas leituras favoritas e aquelas que mais a haviam decepcionado.

Ao citar o diário como sua pior leitura e justificar a escolha com a palavra "vitimista", a entrevista provocou uma onda de reações nas redes sociais.

O Museu do Holocausto e a Federação Israelita divulgaram notas de repúdio à declaração. As duas instituições ressaltaram que o diário precisa ser compreendido dentro do contexto em que foi escrito: o relato de uma adolescente judia que viveu escondida durante a perseguição nazista na Holanda.

As entidades afirmaram ainda que narrar o próprio sofrimento não define uma pessoa apenas pela condição de vítima e destacaram a dimensão histórica do texto, escrito durante um dos períodos mais violentos do século 20.

Mas quem foi Anne Frank? Como era a vida no esconderijo onde ela escreveu? E como aquelas páginas, produzidas por uma adolescente de 13 a 15 anos, se transformaram em um dos livros mais lidos do mundo?

Diário teve quatro versões, sendo a segunda uma revisão feita pela própria Anne com esperança de ter seu relato publicado — Foto: Anne Frank Museum

Annelies Marie Frank nasceu em Frankfurt, na Alemanha, em 12 de junho de 1929. Filha de Otto e Edith Frank, ela tinha uma irmã, Margot, três anos mais velha.

A família era judia e deixou a Alemanha em 1933, após a ascensão do Partido Nazista e a chegada de Adolf Hitler ao poder. Os Frank se mudaram para Amsterdã, na Holanda, onde Anne passou a frequentar a escola, aprendeu holandês e fez novos amigos.

A segurança que encontraram no país, porém, duraria pouco. Em 10 de maio de 1940, a Alemanha invadiu a Holanda. A ocupação foi acompanhada por uma série de medidas antissemitas, que restringiam a vida dos judeus e aumentavam progressivamente sua perseguição.

Otto Frank tentou emigrar para os Estados Unidos, mas não conseguiu concluir o processo antes do fechamento dos consulados americanos nos territórios ocupados pelos alemães.

Em julho de 1942, Margot recebeu uma convocação para se apresentar a um campo de trabalhos forçados. A família decidiu então se esconder. Anne tinha 13 anos.

O 'anexo secreto' onde Anne e sua família se escondeu durante a Segunda Guerra ficava atrás de uma prateleira de livros em prédio de Amsterdã — Foto: Reuters

A família foi para um espaço escondido nos fundos do prédio onde funcionavam os negócios de Otto Frank, no número 263 da Prinsengracht, em Amsterdã. A entrada ficava atrás de uma estante especialmente construída para esconder o acesso.

O local, que Anne chamava de "anexo secreto", tinha cerca de 120 metros quadrados.

Além dos quatro integrantes da família Frank, ali se esconderam Hermann e Auguste van Pels e o filho deles, Peter, além do dentista Fritz Pfeffer.

Durante o dia, quando os funcionários do armazém estavam trabalhando, os oito moradores precisavam evitar qualquer ruído que pudesse revelar sua presença. Não podiam usar água corrente, dar descarga ou conversar normalmente. Risadas, tosses e espirros também precisavam ser contidos.

Anne passava as manhãs estudando e lendo. Depois do almoço, costumava ligar o rádio para acompanhar as notícias — inclusive as transmissões da BBC.

Quatro funcionários de confiança de Otto — Miep Gies, Johannes Kleiman, Victor Kugler e Bep Voskuijl — ajudavam a levar comida, roupas e outros suprimentos para os clandestinos.

Foi nesse ambiente de medo, silêncio e confinamento que Anne escreveu a maior parte de seu diário.

No dia 12 de junho de 1942, quando completou 13 anos, Anne ganhou de presente de Otto um livro de autógrafos de capa de pano xadrez. Ela decidiu transformá-lo em diário.

Na primeira anotação, escrita naquele mesmo dia, disse que esperava poder confiar no caderno como nunca havia conseguido confiar em ninguém e passou a escrever como se conversasse com uma amiga íntima.

O diário registrava o que acontecia no esconderijo, mas ia muito além da guerra.

Anne escrevia sobre as brigas entre os moradores, sua relação com os pais e a irmã, amizades, mudanças em seu corpo, sexualidade, sentimentos por Peter, livros, natureza e seus sonhos para o futuro.

Ela queria se tornar escritora ou jornalista.

Em uma das passagens mais conhecidas, descreveu sua sensação de confinamento comparando-se a um pássaro com as asas cortadas, que se atira contra as grades de uma gaiola.

Mais de 35 milhões de exemplares do diário de Anne Frank já foram vendidos no mundo — Foto: AFP via Getty Images

4. Quem era Kitty, para quem Anne escrevia?

Kitty não era uma colega de escola nem uma amiga imaginária de Anne. O nome era de uma personagem da série infantojuvenil Joop ter Heul , escrita pelo autor holandês Setske de Haan sob o pseudônimo de Cissy van Marxveldt.

No começo, Anne direcionava seus textos a diferentes personagens da série. Mais tarde, passou a escrever principalmente para Kitty.

A mudança aconteceu depois que ela ouviu pelo rádio o ministro da Educação do governo holandês no exílio, Gerrit Bolkestein, defender a preservação de diários, cartas e outros documentos produzidos durante a guerra.

Anne então decidiu reescrever parte de seus textos pensando em uma futura publicação.

Em 29 de março de 1944, registrou no diário uma ideia que a empolgava: transformar a experiência no esconderijo em um livro sobre o "anexo secreto".

Ela não teria tempo de concluir o projeto.

Não. Existem quatro versões principais do texto, identificadas pelas letras A, B, C e D.

A versão A é o manuscrito original de Anne. A versão B corresponde à reescrita que ela própria começou a fazer em 1944, pensando em transformar os registros em um livro.

Já a C foi organizada por Otto Frank para a publicação de 1947. Nessa edição, ele retirou ou resumiu trechos que considerava desnecessários, incluindo passagens sobre a sexualidade de Anne e críticas à mãe, Edith.

Já a versão D, preparada pela escritora e tradutora alemã Mirjam Pressler e publicada em 1995, recuperou trechos retirados da edição de Otto e ampliou o texto. A chamada "edição definitiva" tem mais de 700 páginas.

Por isso, o texto que milhões de pessoas conhecem como O Diário de Anne Frank é resultado de um processo de escrita, reescrita e edição.

A última anotação de Anne é de 1º de agosto de 1944. Três dias depois, em 4 de agosto, a Gestapo, como era chamada a polícia secreta oficial da Alemanha nazista, invadiu o esconderijo e prendeu os oito moradores. Até hoje, a razão pela qual o local foi descoberto permanece em debate.

Os escritos de Anne ficaram no esconderijo. Miep Gies e Bep Voskuijl recolheram os cadernos e papéis e os guardaram.

Otto Frank foi o único dos oito moradores do anexo a sobreviver à guerra. Depois de retornar a Amsterdã e descobrir que a mulher e as filhas haviam morrido, recebeu os textos de Anne.

Inicialmente, ele não conseguia lê-los. A dor era grande demais.

Quando finalmente abriu os diários, Otto descobriu uma faceta da filha que, segundo ele próprio, não conhecia daquela maneira. As páginas mostravam uma adolescente inteligente, expressiva e em processo de amadurecimento, além de revelar seus conflitos familiares, medos, desejos e ambições.

Otto fez cópias do material e mostrou os textos a amigos. Um deles, ligado a uma editora, o convenceu de que o diário não deveria permanecer apenas como um documento privado.

Em 25 de junho de 1947, sob o título Het Achterhuis — ou O Anexo Secreto — foi publicado na Holanda. A primeira tiragem teve pouco mais de 3 mil exemplares.

Nos Estados Unidos, o livro foi lançado em 1952 com o título Anne Frank: The Diary of a Young Girl , ou Anne Frank: O Diário de uma Garota . Antes disso, teve sua publicação recusada por 15 editoras americanas.

Depois de serem presos, os moradores do anexo foram levados para o complexo de campos de concentração Auschwitz-Birkenau. Otto foi separado da mulher e das filhas.

Anne e Margot foram posteriormente transferidas para Bergen-Belsen, na Alemanha. As condições no campo eram extremamente precárias e as duas adoeceram.

Elas morreram de tifo — um grupo de doenças infeciosas e agudas transmitidas através da picada de piolhos, pulgas ou ácaros — em fevereiro de 1945, com poucos dias de diferença. Anne tinha 15 anos.

Uma das últimas pessoas a vê-la com vida foi Nanette Blitz Konig, sua antiga colega no Liceu Judaico de Amsterdã. As duas voltaram a se encontrar em Bergen-Belsen, separadas por uma cerca de arame farpado.

Anne morreu poucas semanas antes de o campo ser libertado por tropas britânicas, em abril de 1945.

Seu corpo e o de Margot foram enterrados em uma vala comum.

Nanette Konig sobreviveu e, mais tarde, se casou e se mudou para São Paulo.

O pai de Anne, Otto, recebeu os diários após a morte dela, em 1945 — Foto: Getty Images

Sim. Mesmo assim, durante décadas o diário foi alvo de alegações de falsificação, sobretudo entre pessoas que negavam ou relativizavam o Holocausto.

Entre as teorias que circularam estava a de que Otto Frank teria escrito os textos da filha. Outras apontavam Miep Gies ou o dramaturgo americano Meyer Levin como possíveis autores.

Especialistas em caligrafia contratados pelo Instituto para Documentação de Guerra examinaram os manuscritos e confirmaram sua autenticidade.

O diário também já foi alvo de tentativas de censura. Em 1983, uma escola no Alabama, nos Estados Unidos, tentou bani-lo por considerá-lo "depressivo". Em 2018, uma escola de Vitória, no Espírito Santo, suspendeu sua leitura depois que trechos foram classificados como "pornográficos".

9. Por que o diário se tornou tão famoso?

Anne morreu aos 15 anos sem ver seu sonho de se tornar escritora realizado. Mas seu relato acabou chegando a milhões de pessoas.

O livro foi traduzido para mais de 70 idiomas e vendeu mais de 35 milhões de exemplares em todo o mundo — cerca de 400 mil deles no Brasil.

A obra também foi adaptada para o teatro, cinema, documentários, quadrinhos, animações e experiências de realidade virtual. Em 1956, a versão teatral recebeu o Prêmio Pulitzer. Três anos depois, a história foi levada às salas de cinema.

Em 1960, o antigo esconderijo da família em Amsterdã foi transformado na Casa de Anne Frank, aberta ao público. O local recebe, em média, cerca de 1,2 milhão de visitantes por ano.

O diário original está preservado e exposto no museu.

A importância da obra está também na perspectiva que ela oferece: em vez de apresentar apenas números e acontecimentos históricos, registra o cotidiano de uma adolescente que continuava estudando, brigando com os pais, se apaixonando, fazendo planos e escrevendo enquanto era perseguida pelos nazistas.

Anne registrou certa vez que queria "continuar vivendo depois da minha morte".

Otto Frank, ao explicar décadas depois por que decidiu publicar os escritos da filha, resumiu o sentido que atribuía àquela frase: por meio do diário, Anne continuaria vivendo na memória e no coração de outras pessoas.

*Por André Bernardo e Myles Burke. Texto escrito a partir de reportagens publicadas originalmente em 11 de junho de 2019, 29 de abril de 2022 e 24 de junho de 2024.

articles.title: Ataque a tiros deixa 3 mortos e 8 feridos em escola nas Filipinas | G1
articles.standfirst: Todas as vítimas eram estudantes com idades entre 14 e 17 anos, e quatro ficaram em estado crítico, segundo governo local. Suspeito era conhecido por fazer piadas e não foi levado a sério quando disse que 'executaria seu plano', afirmou prefeito.
articles.summary: Todas as vítimas eram estudantes com idades entre 14 e 17 anos, e quatro ficaram em estado crítico, segundo governo local. Suspeito era conhecido por fazer piadas e não foi levado a sério quando disse que 'executaria seu plano', afirmou prefeito.
articles.body:
Equipes de emergência em escola em Banga, nas Filipinas, após ataque a tiros em 18 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Cruz Vermelha das Filipinas/Handout via REUTERS

Um ataque a tiros em uma escola no sul das Filipinas nesta sexta-feira (18) deixou três mortos e oito feridos, afirmou o governo local.

Quatro dos oito feridos estavam em estado crítico e todas as vítimas eram estudantes com idades entre 14 e 17 anos, afirmou à Reuters o prefeito da cidade de Banga, Albert Palencia.

O suspeito do ataque tinha 16 anos e está entre os mortos —ele teria atirado contra si mesmo após o ataque, acrescentou o prefeito.

"O suspeito teria se sentado ao lado dos amigos e dito a eles para irem para casa 'porque, depois do almoço, vou executar meu plano'. Os amigos riram porque o atirador era conhecido por fazer piadas. (...) Depois do almoço, ele começou a atirar e atingiu 10 estudantes antes de se matar", disse Palencia à Reuters.

A Cruz Vermelha foi acionada e compareceu à escola junto com a polícia para socorrer as vítimas.

O Departamento de Educação filipino afirmou estar profundamente preocupado com o tiroteio relatado na cidade de Banga, em Cotabato do Sul.

O incidente é o terceiro ataque a tiros em escolas no sul do país desde junho. Tiros em escolas eram raros nas Filipinas até então.

No mês passado, um estudante transmitiu ao vivo o momento em que atirou e matou outro estudante em uma sala de aula em Zamboanga, antes de tirar a própria vida.

Em junho, pelo menos três estudantes foram mortos e cerca de 20 ficaram feridos em um ataque a uma escola pública de ensino médio em Tacloban, onde dois colegas abriram fogo no campus.

O incidente também ocorre após um caso de grande repercussão na Tailândia em agosto, onde um estudante abriu fogo contra uma escola nos arredores da capital Bangkok após ter matado seus avôs em casa.

As Filipinas possuem regulamentações relativamente rigorosas sobre a posse de armas de fogo, incluindo verificação de antecedentes e exigências de avaliação psicológica, embora armas de fogo ilegais continuem em circulação.

articles.title: Fenced-in Matlock woman, 81, wins three-year access fight
articles.summary: Derbyshire County Council shut off a gap, which had been used by a family since 1967.
articles.body:
An 81-year-old has won a three-year battle against a council that fenced across a gap in her garden wall her family had used as access for decades.

Helene Ball - a resident of George Road in Matlock, Derbyshire, since 1967 - took legal action after Derbyshire County Council cemented a metal fence panel blocking the 98cm gated gap between her garden and a council car park in April 2023.

A first-tier tribunal has ruled in Ball's favour over the dispute, after she proved use of the gate since the 1960s.

A right of way has now been established, while the council has been ordered by the courts to pay £50,000 costs and to ensure her access is not impeded again.

Ball, a retired teacher, told the Local Democracy Reporting Service : "I have taught nine, 10 and 11-year-olds all my life, but I never expected the council to act so babyish, they have been spitting their dummies out of the pram and it has been beyond childish.

"They did everything they could to bully me. They tried to put us off but they messed with the wrong ones.

"At my age you don't know how many years you have left, and this has given me three years-plus of stress but now we have proven they blocked our rights."

While the fence panel was removed within a year, vehicle access had been blocked throughout the whole legal battle as the Cavendish Road car park has been on the market for sale as a small housing development.

A route through the site for Ball has now been created by the council using concrete blocks.

The court ruling from Judge Robert Brown said that hired legal representation from the council was "surprisingly combative" and found parts of the legal representation for the council "totally irrelevant" and "most unhelpful".

The council refused to comment on or provide the cost of the legal challenge.

articles.title: Body found in Grand Canyon was missing hiker, wife says, bringing flood death toll to 3
articles.summary: Human remains found in the Grand Canyon this week were those of the last remaining person missing after the deadly flash flooding in late August, the victim’s wife said Thursday.
articles.body: GRAND CANYON NATIONAL PARK, Ariz. — Human remains found in the Grand Canyon this week were those of the last remaining person missing after the deadly flash flooding in late August, the victim’s wife said Thursday. The discovery of Timothy Allen Smith brought the death toll to three from flooding that devastated the Phantom Ranch area at the canyon bottom and damaged the water pipeline serving the South Rim. Smith, 53, was a pilot from western Wyoming’s Star Valley. His remains were found Monday near Crystal Rapids on the Colorado River that runs through the canyon. The remains of Smith’s two backcountry companions, Brent Rosenkranz, 42, and John Giusti, 46, both of Granbury, Texas, were found earlier. Smith grew up in Granbury and lived with his wife in Star Valley Ranch, about 40 miles (64 kilometers) southwest of Jackson. He, Rosenkranz and Giusti were on a multiday hiking, fishing and camping trip when flooding swept through the Grand Canyon. During the two-day deluge, searchers used night vision and other equipment to find people in need of rescue. They relied on the Grand Canyon National Park’s permit system and checked vehicle license plates to track those still missing. More than 80 people were rescued. Soon, only Smith was missing. In a Facebook video at the time, his wife, Carrie, and their children thanked people for their support and prayers. On Tuesday morning, Carrie Smith posted on Facebook that the family was aware a body had been found a day earlier and asked others to pray with them. Smith confirmed in a Facebook post on Thursday that the remains had been identified as her husband’s. “My family has done a lot of waiting over the last three weeks … waiting and hoping Tim (Daddy) would come home, waiting and wondering if the remains found were Tim (Daddy),” she wrote. “We no longer have to wait, Tim was found two days ago by the Rangers at Grand Canyon National Park. Not in the way we had hoped, but we know that he was doing something he loved with John and Brent.” She added, “We know that these three men loved the Lord and were a shining light for Him. The impact their lives had on others is still being shown to our families daily.” The Coconino County medical examiner confirmed Smith’s identity, the National Park Service said in a statement Thursday that thanked the searchers and extended condolences to relatives and friends of the three men. The flooding began Aug. 29 during the summer monsoon, or rainy, season when clear skies can quickly give way to thunderstorms and heavy rain. A desert landscape can funnel water from a deluge into sudden torrents that rage down previously dry gullies and canyons. The rain fell on part of a North Rim burn area left after a lightning-caused wildfire in July 2025. The fire destroyed the historic Grand Canyon Lodge, cabins and other structures. Burn areas can worsen flash flooding because there’s less vegetation to absorb runoff. The flooding damaged a pipeline that supplies water to millions of tourists and residents. Insufficient water caused all overnight lodging to be halted until the pipeline could be restored. National Park Service officials said recently that they expected to restore a reliable water supply in the canyon in weeks — not months — after determining most of a near-complete pipeline project was not damaged during the flash flood. Many hiking trails and lodging areas remain closed, and water has been shut off in the inner canyon, prompting advisories that hikers bring their own water or water filtration devices. Another flash flood hit the canyon along Bright Angel Creek and the Colorado River during a storm Wednesday, park officials said. No injuries were reported. Authorities said efforts to minimize personnel in the canyon before the storm, as well as flash flood warnings, enabled crews to reach safety. Damage assessments were underway.

images.caption: Timothy Allen Smith taken during a Smith family trip to Zion National Park in July 2026.

articles.title: Philippines school shooting leaves at least three dead, including gunman
articles.summary: At least eight people were also injured in the country’s third deadly school shooting since June.
articles.body:
At least three people, including a 16-year-old suspected gunman, have been killed and several injured in a shooting at a school in the Philippines.

The attack was reported on Friday in Banga town in ‌South Cotabato, in the southern Philippines. It is the country’s third deadly school shooting incident since June.

A disaster agency worker reported that two of those killed were students, adding that several others were being treated in hospital. Four of the eight ⁠injured were in ⁠critical condition, and all of the victims were ⁠students aged ⁠14 to ⁠17.

The suspected gunman reportedly shot himself following the attack, South Cotabato provincial governor Reynaldo Tamayo said. Town mayor Albert Palencia later reported that the attacker had died, according to the Reuters news agency.

However, it was not immediately clear how many attackers were involved.

A teacher was heard in a video circulating across social media saying there were two attackers.

“For now, we are trying to let our fellow citizens know that the situation is stable and the case is contained,” Tamayo said. “We never thought this would happen.

“The suspect supposedly sat beside his friends and told them to go home ‘because after lunch, I will be executing my plan’. His friends laughed because the shooter was a known joker,” Palencia said.

“After lunch, he started shooting students. He hit 10 students before killing himself,” Palencia added.

The attack is the third school shooting to take place in the country in recent months.

In August, a student livestreamed himself killing another student and then taking his own life in a classroom in Zamboanga, also in the south of the archipelagic country in Southeast Asia.

Three students were killed and 20 others injured in an attack in June at a public high school in Tacloban , in central Philippines, after two students opened fire.

Nationwide shooter drills were recently conducted in an effort to strengthen school security. But Tamayo urged parents to keep guns out of the reach of minors, saying security personnel are not enough.

“We need to be responsible in storing ‌firearms,” the mayor said. “We cannot expect a handful of security personnel ‌to ‌monitor thousands of students.”

The Philippines has also tightened its gun ownership regulations in response to the tragedies that have spread throughout the country.

Background checks and psychological evaluations have become a requirement for buying a firearm. However, many illegal firearms remain in circulation.

images.caption: The shooting is the third at a Philippines school in recent months [File: AFP]

articles.title: China vessel rams Philippine boat on refueling mission, coast guard says
articles.summary: A China Coast Guard vessel rammed a Philippine boat on a resupply mission in the South China Sea on Friday, damaging its railings and deck structures but causing no injuries, the Philippine Coast Guard said, in the latest confrontation between the two countries in disputed waters.
articles.body: MANILA, Philippines — A China Coast Guard vessel rammed a Philippine boat on a resupply mission in the South China Sea on Friday, damaging its railings and deck structures but causing no injuries, the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) said, in the latest confrontation between the two countries in disputed waters. The Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources vessel BRP Datu Magat Salamat was on a mission to distribute fuel to Filipino fishermen about 54 nautical miles off the coast of Palawan province when a China Coast Guard vessel carried out a series of dangerous maneuvers and made contact with the Philippine ship, the coast guard said. “The China Coast Guard deliberately rammed a civilian government vessel on a humanitarian and livelihood mission,” it said in a statement. Video released by the PCG showed crew members shouting “brace for impact!” moments before the collision, which took place at 11:13 a.m. (11:13 p.m. Thursday ET). Photographs taken after the impact showed bent and detached railings, damaged metal supports and debris scattered across the deck. The China Coast Guard said in a statement that it carried out law enforcement operations in the waters near Sabina Shoal on Friday, after the Philippine vessel “disregarded repeated solemn warnings, deliberately altered its course and suddenly accelerated to cut across the bow of our vessel.” It said the Chinese boat had operated professionally and that the blame for the collision lay with the Philippine side. In July, Manila accused Beijing of firing water cannon ‌at government vessels near the Scarborough Shoal and striking a Philippine Navy staff member on the head with a wooden baton during an encounter in the Second Thomas Shoal.

images.caption: A China Coast Guard ship is seen from the Philippine Coast Guard vessel BRP Cabra in the South China Sea, on Aug.  26, 2024.

articles.title: Indonesia acquires first aircraft carrier amid military upgrade
articles.summary: Indonesia says vessel will be used to aid disaster relief across the archipelago.
articles.body:
Indonesia has welcomed the delivery of its first-ever aircraft carrier with a military ceremony as the vessel arrived at a naval base.

The 41-year-old former Italian navy vessel Giuseppe Garibaldi docked in North Jakarta’s Tanjung Priok seaport on Friday, after sailing from Italy via Colombo and the Malacca strait, Indonesian Navy Chief of Staff Muhammad Ali told reporters.

Indonesia’s President Prabowo Subianto says the ship will be used to manage disasters across the archipelago. However, it arrives amid a drive to upgrade the military.

The 180-metre (590-foot) vessel can carry up to 18 helicopters and accommodate up to 830 personnel, a navy spokesperson said in a statement.

The carrier will be renamed KRI Sriwijaya, honouring the Srivijaya empire, a maritime kingdom based in Sumatra that became one of Southeast Asia’s dominant naval and trading powers between the seventh and 13th centuries.

“There are many disasters in this country. So we really need a vessel or platform that could carry many helicopters, because the helicopters can drop logistics quickly to remote areas,” Ali said.

However, he also noted that the ship could “be deployed for combat missions if necessary”.

The arrival of the vessel, which was commissioned by the Italian navy in 1985, comes as Prabowo has been pushing to upgrade Indonesia’s military assets and build closer defence cooperation with other countries.

Italy agreed to give Indonesia the carrier in March, after it was retired in 2014. The move was meant to bolster the two countries’ defence engagement.

Italy is seeking deals on submarines and aircraft, and gifting the carrier to Indonesia also saves it the cost of decommissioning the ship.

“Its condition is still very good and hopefully it can be used by the Indonesian navy for the next 15 to 20 years,” navy chief Ali said.

Indonesia’s Finance Ministry approved $450m in financing for the aircraft carrier programme in 2025. Opposition politicians worry the overall bill could be far higher.

However, Prabowo – formerly a general under the Suharto regime – has made building Indonesia’s defence assets and agreements a priority.

Jakarta signed an $8.1bn deal in 2022, when Prabowo was defence minister, to purchase 42 French-made Rafale fighter jets. India confirmed this year that it will supply the country with long-range missiles.

Indonesia has also agreed this year to a “Major Defence Cooperation Partnership” with the Trump administration in the United States, and a security treaty with Australia.

articles.title: Three students killed in Philippine school shooting, including gunman, officials say
articles.summary: At least one person was killed and four others injured in a shooting at a high school in the southern Philippines on Friday, the provincial governor said.
articles.body: MANILA, Philippines — Three students were killed in a school shooting in the southern Philippines on Friday, including a 16-year-old suspected gunman who turned the gun on himself, provincial officials said. Eight others were injured, with four in critical condition, and all the victims were students aged 14 to 17, said Albert Palencia, mayor of Banga town in South Cotabato, where the shooting took place. The incident follows two fatal gun incidents since June at schools in the Philippines, where school shootings were previously rare. “The suspect supposedly sat beside his friends and told them to go home ‘because after lunch, I will be executing my plan’. His friends laughed because the shooter was a known joker,” Palencia told Reuters. “After lunch, he started shooting students. He hit 10 students before killing himself,” Palencia added. Last month, a student live-streamed himself shooting and killing another student in a classroom in Zamboanga in the country’s south before taking ‌his own life. In June, at least three students were killed and about 20 others injured in an attack at a public high school in Tacloban, where two classmates opened fire on campus. The Philippines has relatively strict gun ownership regulations, including background checks and psychological evaluation requirements, although illegal firearms remain in circulation. The Friday shooting also follows a high-profile incident in Thailand in August, where a student went on a shooting rampage at a school on the outskirts of the capital Bangkok. South Cotabato governor Reynaldo Tamayo urged parents to ensure guns were kept out of reach of minors. “We need to be responsible in storing firearms. Gun owners, in particular, must make sure that minors do not have access to them,” Tamayo told Reuters by phone. “We cannot expect a handful of security personnel to monitor thousands of students. We need to work together because otherwise this will be very difficult for us to address.”

articles.title: Anthropic says its model Claude is helping to build the next version of itself
articles.summary: Anthropic’s Claude is helping the company develop the next, more intelligent version of the model, the artificial intelligence lab said in an announcement Thursday.
articles.body: Anthropic’s Claude is helping the company develop the next, more intelligent version of the model, the artificial intelligence lab said in an announcement Thursday. Claude is leading 26% of Anthropic’s model research and development, which the company said means it can complete most of a given task “end-to-end from a high-level prompt” while still being under human supervision. The model is not yet working completely autonomously. Still, about 90% of the company’s research and development is done in “collaboration” with Claude, which Anthropic said means the model can do “large chunks of work under close human direction.” The announcement came as some leading figures in AI, led in large part by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, are calling for a slowdown in the technology’s development over safety concerns. As leaders consider pacing AI’s development, “we should do everything possible to minimize the gap between what frontier labs know and what the public knows,” the company said in a blog post. “This means better measuring the development of AI, reporting on it publicly, and giving society an opportunity to decide how to use this information.” The company said that models accelerating their own development could make it “more challenging for humans to understand or control these systems.” It argued that sharing these metrics could lead to better understanding of how close leading AI labs are to reaching recursive self-improvement, or a model’s ability to autonomously build its successor. Anthropic also urged other AI developers to share similar metrics on a regular basis, encouraging the use of a public methodology so the numbers could be compared over time, and potentially across labs. It was unclear from Anthropic’s disclosure how close the company believes it is to achieving recursive self-improvement, but the pace at which Claude has increasingly contributed to research and development is notable. The portion of work Claude “leads,” or does in large part while remaining under human supervision, was none in February. Six months later, it was leading a quarter of research and development work, reaching that benchmark in August. The company also shared details of agent oversight measures it has in place, noting that there were approximately 30,000 agents doing research and engineering work as of August. Oversight measures are crucial for seeing how often agent misbehavior is detected by monitoring systems, the company said. Anthropic recently committed to setting up external third-party evaluators who will be embedded within the company to monitor safety efforts. An Anthropic researcher kicked off much of the recent dialogue around AI safety when he resigned last week with a dire warning about the threats the technology poses to humanity. Amodei, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Elon Musk and other tech leaders have since supported the idea of slowing down development, but other tech leaders and President Donald Trump have pushed back.

articles.title: Australia’s new visa rules will force backpackers to join a lottery to stay longer
articles.summary: French backpacker Zoe has been waiting tables in Australia for months. But a rule change announced by the government means it won’t guarantee she can stay for a third year.
articles.body: French backpacker Zoe has been waiting tables for months. By doing so, she’s trying to earn the right to stay in Australia for a third year, which she hoped would give her the ability to relax and see more of the country. But under a rule change announced by the government on September 17, even working the 88 days per year required for a new working holiday visa won’t be enough. For the chance to secure a third year, she’d have to pay hundreds of dollars to enter the ballot to possibly win one of just 5,000 visas – down from the 31,000 previously granted. “Everyone is stressing out,” said Zoe, 25, who asked that CNN use her first name only. “Everyone’s talking about that. The mood is low.” It’s not just backpackers who are concerned about a premature end to their Australian adventure. Tourism operators and the farming industry are in uproar over the loss of visitors – and vital workers – in regional areas that don’t necessarily have the same appeal to tourists as some of Australia’s major cities. Farmers rely on them to pick fruit and mend fences, the kind of work that requires minimal training but is vital to the operation of businesses in areas where few people live. The government says it’s about adjusting the intake to favor skilled migrants like construction workers; doctors and nurses; experts in agriculture and resources; and law enforcement officers, who are seen to bring more value to the country’s economy. But others say the outcome could be a steep drop in regional workers as first-year backpackers decide that attempting to stay longer isn’t worth it. Relaxed rules for Brits Travel industry insiders say the upheaval didn’t start with Thursday’s announcement, but two years ago, when the rules changed under an Australia-UK free trade agreement. The deal allowed British backpackers to stay for two or three years without having to do 88 days of regional work. It also raised the age limit from 30 to 35. Since then, the number of British young people on working holiday visas has more than doubled to close to 80,000 from a previous peak of 35,000, according to Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke. On Thursday, he described the surge as a “challenge” that his colleagues would be discussing with their UK counterparts in a “constructive way.” In the meantime, the government has adopted a “go-slow” strategy on visa approvals – one that came in July without warning, said Matthew Heyes, founder of the Backpacker Job Board. “The home affairs website wasn’t updated,” he said. “It still said that visas typically get processed in two to three days.” Instead, it took weeks, then months. “We’re seeing backpackers that applied for their visa in July onwards, not having their visas processed still today,” he said. CNN has reached out to the Department of Home Affairs for clarity on how the changes may affect backpackers already in the country. Burke said on Thursday that processing times would return to normal, but Heyes said that doesn’t help the backpackers who have held off booking flights and tours, and the employers who were waiting, ready to hire them, for the harvest season. The government says they have the option to hire laborers under the Pacific Labour Mobility program, a scheme designed to allow Pacific islanders to support families back home. Why the change? The government’s been under pressure from rival parties over immigration levels which surged after Australia lifted its pandemic restrictions and opened the doors to new arrivals. Since then, higher interest rates, a housing shortage, and cost-of-living crisis have contributed to discontent over migration levels – and calls by some for a permanent cut. It’s been an issue championed by the right-wing One Nation party led by Pauline Hanson, who has long held an anti-immigration stance and whose popularity is rising in public opinion polls. The changes announced Thursday will see international students barred from bringing family members, and tougher policing of people who’ve overstayed their visas. By cutting the number of working holiday visas, critics say, the government risks causing more economic pain. As well as slashing the number of third-year visas to 5,000, the number of second-year visas is being cut from 57,000 to 45,000. The total drop over the two years is 38,000 visa places. The Mahony Group runs three pubs and five backpacker hostels around Australia, from Melbourne in the state of Victoria to Cairns in the far north. General manager Max Gibson said his forward bookings were already tracking 25% lower for the rest of the year, and the new visa rules will make it worse. “A lot of our members have said the same – that the last two months have been the worst they’ve experienced since Covid,” said Gibson, who’s also vice president of Youth Tourism Victoria, an industry body that advocates for young travelers. It’s unclear what the new rule change means for backpackers already in the country – some of whom have already been working towards the required 88 days. Laura, 28, from northern France, says she’s worked for three months as a commercial cleaner so far this year with hopes to stay for a third year, then hopefully find a permanent sponsor. “We are doing what Australians don’t want to do,” she said, asking CNN to use one name for privacy. “Not all the Australians want to go to the bush and work in the middle of nowhere. We do it because we want to stay.” “It’s not easy to be backpacker,” said Laura. “It’s not like simple life… we don’t have a really home… our life is just in a backpack.” Zoe said she was working hard with the promise that it would pay off later. “I knew that it was worth it because I would like to get my third year without any problem and be able to enjoy it. But now I’m not even sure about that anymore,” she said. “That’s a bit stressful, and I’m asking, what am I doing all that for?”

articles.title: Iranians rally by the hundreds of thousands in biggest show of defiance since war began
articles.summary: Hundreds of thousands of Iranians rallied Friday in a government-organized show of defiance after months of war, pledging their readiness to take up arms in...
articles.body:
CAIRO (AP) — Hundreds of thousands of Iranians rallied Friday in a government-organized show of defiance after months of war, pledging their readiness to take up arms in the biggest such demonstration since the United States and Israel attacked in February.

Iran's government has sought to rally the people and stress national unity, even as the economy worsens under a U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports and new U.S. sanctions. On Friday, it claimed another attack on a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz , a key waterway it has sought to control since the start of the war.

Estimates varied of the number of people volunteering to receive limited military training and defend the country in an effort described as "Janfaday-e Iran," or the "ones who sacrifice their lives for Iran." They marched through downtown Tehran in combat uniform, carrying flags, as onlookers cheered.

For days, state media have encouraged Iranians to join the campaign, saying training with assault rifles would begin soon. The volunteers would be an additional layer of security to the paramilitary Revolutionary Guard and the Basij militia , which has played a key role in quashing anti-government protests .

Rally seeks to project strength under US pressure

Tehran's Guard chief, Gen. Hassan Hassanzadeh, told the state broadcaster that over 600,000 people had registered to participate, with over 1 million expected to take part in the training. On Friday morning, the broadcaster estimated over 300,000 people were on the streets.

The new head of the Basij, Hossein Taeb , declared in a speech as the rally began that the volunteers will be ready for "full-fledged defense" and similar rallies will take place in other cities soon.

The new trainees will make a "nightmare" for Iran's enemies, Taeb added, as President Masoud Pezeshkian, military commanders and other senior officials watched the march.

Some participants trampled flags of the U.S. and Israel. Others chanted "Death to America" and "Death to Israel."

"I am here to tell (U.S. President Donald) Trump that we Iranians have no fear about his threats against our homeland," said Marzieh Afaghi, 24, who attended the rally with her toddler and husband. "No one in history could invade Iran and remain there."

The rally was also a chance for Iran to show off military hardware. Anti-aircraft batteries were on display, while female Guard members in black headscarves sat with truck-mounted machine guns.

Iran says it attacked another tanker in the Strait of Hormuz

The Guard displayed drones that have been used against ships in the Strait of Hormuz , where Iran's attacks and threats have severely affected the Gulf region's shipments of oil and natural gas to the rest of the world.

Iran said it had attacked a Togo-flagged oil tanker, the Trend, for what it called an "illegal attempt" to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, the state broadcaster reported. The U.K. Maritime Trade Operations center said a tanker was hit by a projectile, sparking a fire on board that was extinguished.

The UKMTO in a separate update said ship transits facilitated by the U.S. military off Oman have averaged 24 a day over the past week but overall traffic remains about 90% lower than before the war.

Iran's new volunteers could help suppress future dissent

Friday's events also suggested that hard-liners like Taeb among Iran's leadership will be more prepared to suppress any future demonstration against the theocracy.

In January, shortly before the war, Iran saw some of its largest nationwide protests in history, which began over the struggling economy and turned to wider grievances. Activists have said a crackdown killed over 7,000 people and saw tens of thousands detained.

In May, government officials said more than 30 million people in Iran — which has a total population of some 90 million — had volunteered via an online form or at public gatherings to lay down their lives for the theocracy. The Associated Press could not independently confirm that.

Karimi reported from Tehran, Iran, and Anna from Jerusalem.

articles.title: Philippines: Three dead and eight injured in shooting at Banga high school
articles.summary: The gunman is among the dead in what is the third school shooting in the country since June.
articles.body:
A 16-year-old gunman has shot two students dead and injured eight others at a Philippine high school, before killing himself.

The two deceased victims were 14-year-old pupils at a school in Banga in the southern province of Mindanao, the local mayor told the BBC.

Albert Palencia said four of the injured were in critical condition.

The education department said in a statement it was "deeply concerned" by the reported incident which took place on Friday afternoon at Banga National High School.

This is the third deadly school shooting in the Philippines since June this year.

"Our immediate priority is the safety and well-being of our learners, teachers and school personnel," the education department said, adding it was coordinating with authorities to verify the incident and provide necessary support.

"We urge everyone to remain calm and refrain from sharing unverified information as authorities continue their investigation."

Palencia told Reuters news agency that during a lunchtime conversation on Friday, the gunman had urged friends to go home "because after lunch, [he would] be executing [his] plan".

"His friends laughed because the shooter was a known joker," Palencia told the news agency.

"After lunch, he started shooting students. He hit 10 students before killing himself."

Classes have been suspended "in all levels in the entire municipality of Banga" due to the shooting, disaster management authorities said in a statement.

The Philippines Red Cross said it was alerted to the incident at 14:00 local time (06:00 GMT) and had dispatched an ambulance with four paramedics to provide life-saving assistance.

Police are at the site investigating the shooting, local media reported.

Gun crime is not uncommon in the Philippines, which has one of the highest rates of gun ownership in the region. Broadly speaking, school shootings are rare, but today's incident marks the third deadly campus shooting in the last four months.

In June, three students were killed and more were injured after their peers opened fire at a high school in central Philippines. Investigators believed the deadly shooting had been motivated by a "grudge" over bullying.

In August, a student at a Catholic junior high school in the southern Philippines shot dead a fellow student and later took his own life. In this case, the suspect had fired at the teacher, but missed, then moved to another classroom and shot a student, who later died.

Following the shooting on Friday, Reynaldo Tamayo, the South Cotabato governor, urged adult gun owners to "be responsible in storing firearms" and ensuring that minors do not get access to them.

"We cannot expect a handful of security personnel to monitor thousands of students. We need to work together because otherwise this will be very difficult for us to address," he told Reuters.

articles.title: A painter paid $192,000 for a 1902 lighthouse three miles offshore; now he wants to turn the abandoned structure into a destination
articles.summary: Rest of World News: For more than a century, the 1902 Hooper Island Lighthouse has stood three miles offshore in Maryland’s Chesapeake Bay. Years of exposure have left th.
articles.body: For more than a century, the 1902 Hooper Island Lighthouse has stood three miles offshore in Maryland’s Chesapeake Bay. Years of exposure have left the historic structure badly in need of repair, but its latest owner sees an opportunity to give it a new purpose. Pennsylvania painter Rich Cucé paid $192,000 for the abandoned lighthouse after competing against several other bidders. The building has no running water, heat or electricity and faces major restoration challenges. Cucé hopes to repair the landmark and eventually create a destination focused on the Chesapeake Bay and its wildlife.How the $192,000 lighthouse entered the life of a painterThe Hooper Island Lighthouse was built as a navigation aid at a time when ships depended on lighthouses to travel safely through the Chesapeake Bay. According to SpinSheet, the lighthouse was completed in 1902, when keepers had to work around the clock, lighting the lamp with oil and watching for ice, fog and other vessels. As navigation technology improved and many lighthouse duties became automated, structures that were difficult to reach were increasingly left without the care.This 4-storey white tower is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and has a watch room and lantern at the top. The Associated Press(AP) reported that the light still operates using solar power, meaning the lighthouse continues to serve its original navigational purpose even though the building around it has deteriorated.The federal government eventually put the property up for auction. AP reported that the bidding started at $15,000 before rising through $38,000 and $189,000. Five anonymous bidders were interested, and the final price reached $192,000. The buyer was later identified as Cucé, an industrial painter from Bucks County, Pennsylvania.The abandoned lighthouse presented major challenges for its new ownerThe price of the lighthouse was only the beginning. AP News reported the structure without running water, heating or electricity, while lead paint, asbestos and benzene added to the problems facing its new owner. Vandals had damaged the entrance, birds had occupied parts of the building and rust had affected the tower and its cast-iron foundation. A 2019 Coast Guard inspection found the lighthouse in fair condition but approaching poor condition.Its location makes almost every repair more complicated. The tower rises from water about three miles from land, and the surrounding area is also a U.S. Navy testing site. Cucé had to agree to stay away during weapons testing. According to SpinSheet, he expected travelling to and from the lighthouse, particularly in rough weather, to be among the hardest parts of the work.Access was one of the first practical issues to address. As reported by SpinSheet, Cucé said an inspection would come first, followed by plans for a dock that could make it easier to reach the lighthouse and provide a place to bring equipment and materials ashore.Rich Cucé brought his painting experience to the lighthouse restorationCucé’s professional background gives him a direct connection to the work. AP News reported that he had operated an industrial painting and sandblasting business since the mid-1990s, working on structures including train cars and roller coasters. He had experience restoring and rebuilding old houses. For him, the lighthouse presented a challenge that matched skills he had developed over decades.The exterior was expected to be one of the more familiar parts of the job. His plan was to restore the structure while keeping the work environmentally responsible.The restoration also had to follow conditions attached to the purchase. WBOC reported that Cucé must maintain the lighthouse as a Coast Guard navigation aid, follow historic preservation standards and comply with an agreement with the U.S. Navy governing when he can be at the site.The restored lighthouse could become an environmental destinationWBOC reported that Cucé wanted the lighthouse to become a place where members of the community could study about the Chesapeake Bay while gaining a better understanding of the need to protect it.He also wanted environmental groups to use the restored lighthouse to monitor water quality and marine life. AP News noted that the structure sits near an area of oxygen-depleted water known as a dead zone, giving the proposed centre an especially relevant setting for environmental work.AP News reported that he wanted to hire watermen from the three Hoopers Islands to help with the restoration. He considered a range of future possibilities, including tours, special events, sunset cruises, weddings and yoga retreats.The tower itself is relatively compact, with about 65 feet between the waterline and the light, and small rooms inside. The plans give the abandoned structure a possible second life, not only as a preserved piece of Chesapeake history, but as a destination centred on the Bay itself.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
